page: Amazon Web Services r5dn.4xlarge is a memory-optimized Nitro-based virtual machine configured with 16 vCPUs and 128 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz. Driven by an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor clocked at 3.1 GHz across 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading, the instance delivers an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Hardware features include 600 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and a 16 Gbps baseline network interface. Discrete GPU accelerators are not present. Instruction set support includes AVX-512 with VNNI for vectorized arithmetic alongside hardware-assisted AES cryptography.

Benchmark evaluations place the instance in the middle tier of cloud compute for multi-threaded workloads, achieving a multi-core stress-ng score of 13544.88 and a Geekbench multi-core result of 7031.0. Large-block memory bandwidth sustains 88.79 GB/sec for reads and 47.79 GB/sec for writes. Redis throughput reached 13.59 million SET operations per second, reflecting solid memory responsiveness. In contrast, single-thread performance benchmarks register in the lower quartile, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 1133.0 and reduced speeds in single-threaded compression tests.

From an infrastructure perspective, bundled high-speed local NVMe storage and substantial memory density provide qualitative cost efficiency for workloads requiring low-latency scratch space without relying entirely on remote network storage volumes. The primary technical tradeoff centers on modest single-thread execution rates compared to newer processor architectures. The hardware profile aligns directly with memory-intensive workloads, including distributed in-memory caching tiers, relational database hosting with local temp space requirements, and analytical ETL processing.
description: Amazon Web Services r5dn.4xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, offering 16 vCPUs and 128 GB of DDR4 memory across an 8-core Intel Xeon 8259CL processor clocked at 3.1 GHz. Designed for data-intensive processing, the configuration includes 600 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and 16 Gbps baseline network throughput without discrete GPU hardware. Benchmark results indicate balanced mid-tier multi-threaded compute and memory bandwidth, delivering 13.59 million Redis SET operations per second and 88.79 GB/sec uncached memory read throughput. While single-threaded performance is lower relative to current-generation alternatives, the 8 GB per vCPU density combined with onboard NVMe storage provides practical hardware efficiency. This server is suited for in-memory databases, Redis caching layers, search indexing, and relational database workloads utilizing local scratch disks.
